references.text: Joseph's brothers react to their father Jacob's favoritism toward Joseph by tearing off the special tunic (ketonet passim) he had received.
Joseph's brothers dip his tunic in goat blood to deceive their father into believing that Joseph is dead.
Judah tells Joseph that Benjamin is a son of his father's old age, mirroring the description of Joseph as 'a son of his old age' (ben-zequnim).
Isaac loved Esau while Rebekah loved Jacob—favoritism toward children is a recurring theme in the patriarchal narratives, here repeated with Jacob's favoritism toward Joseph.
Jacob's special love for Joseph is connected to his deep love for Rachel, Joseph's mother, whom he served seven years for.
Tamar's 'ketonet passim' (tunic with sleeves/many colors) is the only other occurrence of this expression in the OT and describes a special garment worn by royal daughters.
Typological connection: Joseph as the 'beloved son' is a precursor to Christ, the beloved Son who is sent out.
